title: Sonic Temple Puzzle
description: The player stands in a sacred temple (nemetona) where mystical BoomBoxes are scattered across pedestals. Each BoomBox emits a colored energy beam when activated, and the player must route beams through mirrors to unlock the temple's central altar by satisfying energy conservation laws — total beam energy in must equal energy out at every junction node. Supports full undo/redo of all placement and rotation actions.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) implementing a beam-routing puzzle game. Load 'shared_assets/nemetona.glb' as the temple environment scaled to fill the scene, and load 'shared_assets/BoomBox.glb' replicated 5 times, each tinted a unique color (red, blue, green, yellow, purple) and placed on stone pedestals around the temple interior. Camera: perspective at eye-level with OrbitControls, clamped to stay inside the temple. Lighting: warm ambient light plus directional light casting shadows, and colored point lights on each BoomBox matching its tint. Gameplay: clicking a BoomBox toggles it ON/OFF (emitting a colored beam via a RayCaster-visualized cylinder/line). The scene has 4 mirror nodes (flat reflective planes) the player can click-drag to reposition on a grid and rotate in 45-degree increments using mouse wheel. Beams reflect off mirrors realistically. A junction node at the temple center acts as the altar — it displays incoming energy values. Conservation law: each beam carries an energy value (red=3, blue=2, green=4, yellow=1, purple=5). At every mirror node, total incoming energy must equal total outgoing energy (beams split if multiple outputs). The altar unlocks when it receives exactly 10 total energy. HUD overlay shows: current altar energy, target (10), and action history. Implement full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) tracking every toggle, mirror move, and mirror rotation as discrete actions. Minimum solution requires 10-14 steps: toggling specific BoomBoxes, positioning mirrors, rotating them, possibly undoing mistakes. Show a victory particle effect erupting from the altar when solved. All in under one HTML file with inline JS and CSS.
